description: Operational provider health incident dashboard for health-check latency, adapter/API pressure, retry exhaustion, circuit-breaker state, and provider-level failure share.

panels.title: Review Dashboard Navigation
panels.description: Responsive same-tab navigation bus with identical composition and order across all shipped dashboards. It preserves the current time range and supported scope, uses theme-safe normal/hover/focus/active tokens, and wraps predictably at 1024 px. Explore Logs and Explore Traces require the optional tracing profile; traces are available only for traced runs. Alerts keep explicit Global/Pipeline/Run scope.

links.title: 4. Data Quality
links.tooltip: Open the Data Quality dashboard in the same tab.

links.title: 5. Workflow
links.tooltip: Scoped handoff: passes workflow/pipeline/run_type context; Workflow owns its status and step filters.

links.title: 6. Alerts & SLO
links.tooltip: Open the alert surface in the same tab. Global alerts remain explicitly badged and are not attributed to the selected pipeline.

links.title: Silver Reject Explorer
links.tooltip: Context mapping: bounded pipeline/run_type explorer scope. Reset scope: record-level filters remain explorer-owned. Opens in the same tab.

links.title: Explore Logs
links.tooltip: Optional tracing profile adjunct evidence. Zero lines can legitimately mean shipping is disabled or no BioETL streams exist; refine in Explore.

links.title: Explore Traces
links.tooltip: Available only for traced runs. Enable the optional tracing profile with --tracing; this is adjunct evidence, not a headline verdict.

panels.title: Provenance
panels.description: Unified context/provenance banner for 3. Provider Health. Scope: workflow=$workflow, pipeline=$pipeline, run_type=$run_type, run_id=$run_id, selected Grafana time range. Workflow is context/evidence unless documented otherwise; run_id is local control-plane identity context only. Provider health is owned by provider-status telemetry, while ID and Processed Records below are bounded pipeline-context evidence only.

options.content:
Which provider is degraded or failing, and why?
Start with GLOBAL severity + telemetry freshness; selected-provider Status can disagree by design.
Provider-global selected-range: adapter latency and HTTP error panels aggregate by provider and do not filter by run_id/run_type in PromQL. For backfill-specific stage latency or exact-run identity, open 2. Runtime or 0. Control Plane with preserved scope.

panels.title: Status
panels.description: Selected-range provider-first severity for the selected provider. Status mapping: 0=OK, 1=WARN, >=2=CRIT, null=UNKNOWN. Uses bioetl_provider_current_status and bioetl_provider_range_operational_ok inside the active Grafana time range (default Last 12 hours). Operational OK is projected when health-check or adapter request counters show successful provider activity without failures or HTTP errors in range; it does not prove the currently selected pipeline run succeeded, but it prevents UNKNOWN after successful provider operations in range. If both series are absent, UNKNOWN remains fail-closed; inspect Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness and Review Raw Provider Health Enum. Pipeline/run_type/workflow are secondary context only; run_id does not filter Prometheus. This compact Status is selected-provider scope and is intentionally rendered as a supporting selected-provider verdict, not as the visual owner of the fleet answer. GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix and Critical Providers are global fleet posture and may disagree by design. Do not compare the selected-provider OK card to a GLOBAL WARN/CRIT panel without reading the scope labels.

panels.title: ID
panels.description: Compact two-column local control-plane identity table. Shows Run ID, Manifest ID, Provider.Entity [Version], Contract [Schema], Execution, execution flags, Replay [Capability.Mode], Checkpoint [Anchors], optional Composite Run, and Identity Health. Exact selected run_id wins; aggregate pipeline scope without exact run_id must not guess one manifest identity; values come from HTTP, not Prometheus labels. This card is bounded pipeline/run context evidence only and does not prove current provider health. No data/datasource errors on this HTTP-backed card mean the Quarantine Explorer/control-plane backend may be unavailable; verify /health/live before interpreting the card as expected empty.

defaults.noValue: Not resolved — no identity rows for the selected run/scope. Check backend health (/health/live), then select or reset run_id; this is not a valid empty run.

panels.title: Processed Records
panels.description: Current stage/outcome accounting evidence for the shared pipeline/run_type context. Provider remains the primary health selector; this table is bounded pipeline/run_type accounting evidence and does not prove current provider health by itself. Missing accounting series render UNKNOWN/no data, not OK. Summary status, accounted subtotal, and delta rows are intentionally not displayed in this compact table; use Status, Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness, and detailed recording rules for verdict/delta triage. No data/datasource errors on this HTTP-backed card mean the Quarantine Explorer/control-plane backend may be unavailable; verify /health/live before interpreting the card as expected empty.

defaults.noValue: Not resolved — no processed-record rows. Check backend health and selector scope; backend unavailable is not a valid zero-record state.

panels.title: First Action
panels.description: First operator CTA for global provider incidents and early-warning provider causes. Start with the current GLOBAL severity matrix, then telemetry freshness, then critical providers and top causes. Treat selected-provider Status as supporting scoped evidence; if Status is UNKNOWN, treat that as missing provider-current-status evidence until telemetry freshness and raw enum evidence say otherwise. Use this after the current answer row; selected-range latency/error evidence stays below and downstream Runtime or Control Plane follow-up depends on the diagnosed cause.

options.content:
First Action

1. Read GLOBAL WARN/CRIT and telemetry freshness. 2. Open the top cause/critical provider. 3. Use selected-range cards only as supporting evidence.

panels.description: Provider severity mapping: 0=OK, 1=DEGRADED, 2=FAILING; null/NaN=UNKNOWN. This matrix now uses the active Grafana time selector and shows the most severe observed provider-current-status sample for each provider inside that window. Raw provider health status remains panel id=114 with 0=UNHEALTHY, 1=DEGRADED, 2=HEALTHY. This matrix intentionally stays GLOBAL and does not filter by pipeline. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id, pipeline, run_type, or selected provider unless the panel title says selected provider.
panels.title: Monitor GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix

panels.description: Only providers observed as DEGRADED or FAILING inside the active Grafana time range. Empty table means no provider exceeded OK in the selected window; providers with missing current-status telemetry remain visible as UNKNOWN in the GLOBAL severity matrix. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id, pipeline, run_type, or selected provider unless the panel title says selected provider.
panels.title: Inspect Critical Providers

panels.description: Top provider causes from canonical cause recording rules over the active Grafana time range: raw status, failure rate, retry exhaustion, latency, HTTP errors, or rate-limit pressure. This panel can surface early-warning provider causes even while the GLOBAL severity matrix still reads OK, because the cause projection is evaluated independently from the current-status projection. Empty table means no canonical provider cause rose above zero for any provider in the selected window. If the GLOBAL severity matrix is non-OK while this table stays empty, treat that as a provider explainability gap and inspect the raw status matrix plus optional rate-limit/circuit-breaker evidence before leaving the dashboard. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id, pipeline, run_type, or selected provider unless the panel title says selected provider. The wider first-screen table keeps cause, provider and route readable at 1024 px.

defaults.noValue: No canonical provider causes projected. If critical providers remain visible, treat this as an explainability gap and inspect raw provider status plus optional telemetry.

panels.title: Inspect Provider Top Causes

panels.description: Selected-range provider telemetry freshness marker for the first screen. Status mapping: 0=OK, 1=WARN, >=2=CRIT, null=UNKNOWN. If no bioetl_provider_current_status samples exist inside the active Grafana time range, this panel returns WARN so the empty severity matrix is treated as a telemetry gap, not proof that providers are healthy.
panels.title: Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness
Review Raw Provider Health Enum
panels.description: Raw provider health enum evidence over the active Grafana time range, not the canonical first-screen verdict. Values are source enum: 0=UNHEALTHY, 1=DEGRADED, 2=HEALTHY; null/NaN=UNKNOWN when the provider exists in the selected-range provider universe but raw status is absent. Use this as supporting evidence when Status is UNKNOWN or when top causes and severity disagree. First-screen severity uses bioetl_provider_current_status in the Status and GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix panels to avoid inverting raw enum colors.

defaults.noValue: No provider latency samples in range. This optional telemetry is neutral; use severity, freshness, and raw enum panels for provider verdict.

panels.title: Track Health Check Latency by Provider (p95)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: p95 provider health-check latency over the active Grafana interval. Current provider severity is owned by the GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix.

panels.title: Monitor Healthy Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: completed HEALTHY probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source.

panels.title: Monitor Degraded Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: completed DEGRADED probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source, so non-zero counts remain neutral evidence rather than WARN/CRIT by themselves.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Rate (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: failed probes divided by completed probes in the active Grafana range. Current status comes from bioetl_provider_current_status. Gauge thresholds follow the provider policy contract: warning at 5%, critical at 20%. A 0.00% value is neutral supporting evidence and never renders as a dominant red gauge arc.

targets.expr: round((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Track Health Checks Total (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: total completed provider health checks in the active Grafana range.

Compact optional selected-provider telemetry. Collapsed by the progressive-disclosure contract so empty latency, adapter, rate-limit, and circuit-breaker samples do not dominate the provider verdict; expand it only for selected-provider diagnosis.
panels.title: Selected Provider Detail
Track Failure and Degraded Trend by Provider
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: failure/degraded probe trend over the active Grafana interval.

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Share (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: provider share of failed probes in the active Grafana range. The full share chart is collapsed by default and should be expanded only when total failures are non-zero.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retries exhausted by provider and operation in the active Grafana range. Non-zero rows identify where retry budgets were consumed, not raw provider-health enum state.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted Trend by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retry exhaustion trend by provider and operation over the active Grafana interval. Rising non-zero series point to persistent retry-budget pressure.

defaults.noValue: No optional health-check latency samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Inspect Provider Health Check Latency (p95) - $provider
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: per-provider p95 health-check latency over the active Grafana range. No data means no latency samples or no probe activity in range, not 0s latency and not a provider verdict.

defaults.noValue: No optional adapter latency samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Inspect Adapter Request Latency by Endpoint (p95)
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: p95 adapter request latency by endpoint for the selected provider scope. Provider-global selected-range only; for backfill-specific stage latency open 2. Runtime with preserved pipeline/run_type/run_id scope. No data remains diagnostic and means no endpoint latency samples in range; it does not refute current provider severity.

defaults.noValue: No optional rate-limit error samples in range; not a provider verdict.

targets.expr: round(sum by (provider, method, error_type) (increase(bioetl_http_request_errors_total{provider=~"$provider", error_type=~"(?i).*(rate.?limit|429|thrott).*"}[$__interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Inspect Rate Limit Errors by Method
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range rate-limit pressure from HTTP errors where error_type indicates throttling/rate-limit classes. Empty samples stay diagnostic and do not refute current provider severity. Use alongside Monitor Rate Limiter Wait p95 for provider-global scope.

defaults.noValue: No optional timeout/network samples in range; not a provider verdict.

targets.expr: round(sum by (provider, method, error_type) (increase(bioetl_http_request_errors_total{provider=~"$provider", error_type=~"(?i).*(timeout|timed.?out|network).*"}[$__interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Inspect Network Timeout Errors by Method
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range network/timeout failures separated from rate-limit pressure. Empty samples stay diagnostic and do not refute current provider severity. Provider-global scope; correlate with Runtime stage errors when pipeline handoff context is set.

defaults.noValue: No optional rate-limiter wait samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Track Rate Limiter Wait by Provider (p95)
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: p95 wait time imposed by provider rate limiting. No data means no observed wait samples in range, not a healthy wait time. This optional telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK. The provider degraded-rule surface starts at p95 > 1s; this panel keeps a lower yellow band for earlier-warning inspection.

defaults.noValue: No rate-limiter token samples in range. This remains diagnostic and does not disprove provider pressure.

panels.title: Monitor Minimum Rate Limiter Tokens Available
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: minimum provider tokens available in the active Grafana range. Lower values indicate higher rate-limit pressure; 0 means requests can be blocked. No data remains diagnostic and means no token samples were observed in range. This optional telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK.

defaults.noValue: No circuit-breaker state samples in range. Adapter-scoped telemetry is optional and does not imply CLOSED.

panels.title: Monitor Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker State (max)
panels.description: Compact cross-scope adapter diagnostics over the active Grafana range: 0=CLOSED, 1=HALF_OPEN, 2=OPEN. Uses the adapter selector because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not imply a synthetic CLOSED state. This adapter-scoped telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK.

defaults.noValue: No circuit-breaker trip samples in range. Adapter-scoped telemetry is optional and remains diagnostic.

panels.title: Track Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker Trips
panels.description: Compact cross-scope adapter diagnostics: selected-range circuit-breaker trip count by adapter over the active Grafana interval. This panel is intentionally adapter-scoped because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not create synthetic adapter rows. Empty adapter telemetry does not refute current provider severity on its own.
